set.body:
EventId, ConditionId, FactorId, TermId, ColumnId are five character-for-character copies of the same 'opaque type X = String' + apply/unsafe/value block, differing only in a kind label and an allowDot flag. DesignColumnIndex, ScanIndex, RunIndex, BasisIndex, TermIndex are five copies of the same 'opaque type X = Int' + fromOneBased/fromZeroBased/unsafeOneBased/oneBased/zeroBased block.

That is ~130 of DesignTypes.scala's 190 lines.

The DISTINCTIONS are worth keeping — these are genuinely different types and must not be interchangeable. The DEFINITIONS need not be repeated:

  opaque type DesignId[Tag] = String
  opaque type OneBasedIndex[Tag] = Int

DesignId[Event] and DesignId[Term] remain distinct types; ~130 lines become ~30.

Purely mechanical, but sequence it AFTER the id round-trip fix (bd-01KYYK1VED50YQP6FFSHX099HW), which settles what construction means. Doing it first would just entrench the sanitize-on-parse behaviour in a shared definition.

p3 because it is readability rather than correctness — nothing is wrong today beyond the repetition.

Context: docs/plans/design-hardening.md section 2.4 and phase 4.
set.title: Collapse ten copy-paste opaque id types into two tagged newtypes
